topic: What if Gojo had cremated Geto's body, so Kenjaku never gets the face that sealed him in Shibuya
title: What If Gojo Cremated Geto's Body?
description:
What if Gojo had cremated Geto's body after the Night Parade? Gojo left Geto's body unburned, and Kenjaku used it to wear that face, which froze Gojo long enough for the Prison Realm in Shibuya. We follow that one choice through Shibuya, the Culling Game and Gojo's students.

Is the Prison Realm still possible without Geto's face, or would Kenjaku find a worse way? Tell us your pick, and watch the related story, Gojo wasn't beaten by power, just one familiar face.

lines.text: Now the fallout looks nothing like what we got. No empty Tokyo, no frozen sorcerers, no three year gap.

lines.text: Gojo stays on the board, and the school never loses its anchor. That is the simplest version of the story.

shot.fallback: anime style two young sorcerers in dark school uniforms talking at dusk

lines.text: Think about how bad the real timeline gets once Gojo is gone: a locked down Tokyo, and sorcerers forced into a survival game.

shot.fallback: anime style two young sorcerers in dark school uniforms talking at dusk

lines.text: I'd bet the story would be shorter, louder, and less lonely. I'm not sure it would be better. That's my honest guess.

lines.text: And honestly, that scares me more. Because nothing in the book says Gojo's students are safer than his friend was.

shot.fallback: anime style two young sorcerers in dark school uniforms talking at dusk

lines.text: But that comfort has a cost, and it's the one most fans skip when they imagine a free Gojo...

shot.fallback: anime style two young sorcerers in dark school uniforms talking at dusk

lines.text: Think about what the sealing did to Gojo's students. It forced every one of them to grow up without him.

shot.fallback: anime style two young sorcerers in dark school uniforms talking at dusk

lines.text: Megumi grows up. Yuji grows up. Yuta, trained and hardened, ends up carrying a job he was never meant to carry.

shot.fallback: anime style two young sorcerers in dark school uniforms talking at dusk

lines.text: In canon, Yuta ends up being the one who cuts Kenjaku down, in chapter 243.

shot.fallback: anime style two young sorcerers in dark school uniforms talking at dusk

lines.text: That moment doesn't exist if Gojo is the one who stays at the front line.

lines.text: A free Gojo would also never be unsealed in chapter 221, because there would be nothing to unseal.

lines.text: And the big fight that follows would be built on a different board, with different pieces.

shot.fallback: anime style two young sorcerers in dark school uniforms talking at dusk

shot.fallback: anime style two young sorcerers in dark school uniforms talking at dusk

lines.text: The question is whether anyone stands in front of him with the one thing that actually matters, which is time.

shot.fallback: anime style two young sorcerers in dark school uniforms talking at dusk

lines.text: Gojo with time, and his students beside him, is a different problem than Gojo showing up late. Really, he never does.

shot.fallback: anime style two young sorcerers in dark school uniforms talking at dusk

lines.text: That's the version of this story where the tragedy shrinks and the victory grows. I like that version.

shot.fallback: anime style two young sorcerers in dark school uniforms talking at dusk

lines.text: Gojo's greatest belief is that the next generation will be stronger than he is. He meant every word of it.

shot.fallback: anime style two young sorcerers in dark school uniforms talking at dusk

lines.text: If he stays, that belief gets tested sooner, and I don't think it survives a world where he never steps back.

shot.fallback: anime style two young sorcerers in dark school uniforms talking at dusk

lines.text: This is my least popular opinion about Gojo. The seal was the most useful thing the plot ever did to his students.

shot.fallback: anime style two young sorcerers in dark school uniforms talking at dusk

lines.text: Then Sukuna's return stops being a plot twist and starts being a clock the whole school can watch.

shot.fallback: anime style two young sorcerers in dark school uniforms talking at dusk

lines.text: That's the part a pure power fan misses. The Prison didn't only remove Gojo. It rewired everyone he left behind.

shot.fallback: anime style two young sorcerers in dark school uniforms talking at dusk

lines.text: And still, it isn't a perfect fix. It might even be the worse one...

shot.fallback: anime style two young sorcerers in dark school uniforms talking at dusk

lines.text: Here's what I keep coming back to.

shot.fallback: anime style two young sorcerers in dark school uniforms talking at dusk

lines.text: Gojo didn't lose Shibuya to power. He lost it to love for a friend he could not forget.

shot.fallback: anime style two young sorcerers in dark school uniforms talking at dusk

lines.text: And that same love is the reason the body was left behind in the first place.

shot.fallback: anime style two young sorcerers in dark school uniforms talking at dusk

lines.text: I think Gege Akutami wrote it that way on purpose, so the weakness and the strength share one root.

shot.fallback: anime style two young sorcerers in dark school uniforms talking at dusk

lines.text: Burn the body, and Gojo is safer but a little emptier. Keep it, and the world pays for his heart.

shot.fallback: anime style two young sorcerers in dark school uniforms talking at dusk

lines.text: That's the cruel part. There's no clean answer here, only a choice about which way he breaks.

shot.fallback: anime style two young sorcerers in dark school uniforms talking at dusk

lines.text: Even the story keeps that question open for the reader.

shot.fallback: anime style two young sorcerers in dark school uniforms talking at dusk

lines.text: So I don't think the story is about whether Gojo should have burned the body.

shot.fallback: anime style two young sorcerers in dark school uniforms talking at dusk

lines.text: I think it's about how the strongest man alive was beaten by the one wound no technique can guard.

shot.fallback: anime style two young sorcerers in dark school uniforms talking at dusk

lines.text: That's my read, and I think it explains Shibuya better than any power ranking ever could. Nobody else gets a read like that.

shot.fallback: anime style two young sorcerers in dark school uniforms talking at dusk

lines.text: Because the day Gojo chose to keep his friend whole was the day the trap got built.

shot.fallback: anime style two young sorcerers in dark school uniforms talking at dusk

lines.text: Look at how Akutami frames their last conversation. It isn't a fight scene. It's two old friends in a courtyard.

shot.fallback: anime style two young sorcerers in dark school uniforms talking at dusk

lines.text: Then look at Shibuya. The same silence, the same stare, the same man standing in front of Gojo.

shot.fallback: anime style two young sorcerers in dark school uniforms talking at dusk

lines.text: I know that sounds romantic, and I mean it to be. Gojo is a man defined by what he refused to let go.

shot.fallback: anime style two young sorcerers in dark school uniforms talking at dusk

lines.text: The film handles this with silence. The manga handles it with a body and a decision nobody wanted to make.

shot.fallback: anime style two young sorcerers in dark school uniforms talking at dusk

lines.text: Both versions agree on the cruel point. Gojo chose to keep a piece of Geto, and Geto came back anyway.

shot.fallback: anime style two young sorcerers in dark school uniforms talking at dusk

lines.text: And what if the thing that destroyed him was never a flaw, but the best part of him...

shot.fallback: anime style two young sorcerers in dark school uniforms talking at dusk

lines.text: So let me lay out the whole chain, because I think it's tighter than most What Ifs.

shot.fallback: anime style two young sorcerers in dark school uniforms talking at dusk

lines.text: One. Gojo leaves the body, and Kenjaku takes it.

shot.fallback: anime style two young sorcerers in dark school uniforms talking at dusk

lines.text: Two. Kenjaku gains Geto's technique, memories and face.

shot.fallback: anime style two young sorcerers in dark school uniforms talking at dusk

lines.text: Three. The face stops Gojo for the one minute the Prison needs.

shot.fallback: anime style two young sorcerers in dark school uniforms talking at dusk

lines.text: Four. With Gojo out of play, the Culling Game becomes possible.

shot.fallback: anime style two young sorcerers in dark school uniforms talking at dusk

lines.text: Pull the first link, and every other link needs a different story.

shot.fallback: anime style two young sorcerers in dark school uniforms talking at dusk

lines.text: That's why this is the strongest what if I can build from canon, and not a random alternate universe.

shot.fallback: anime style two young sorcerers in dark school uniforms talking at dusk

lines.text: It uses the story's own rules, its own dates, and one choice Akutami placed there on purpose.

shot.fallback: anime style two young sorcerers in dark school uniforms talking at dusk

lines.text: But Kenjaku ends up in the same corner every time. He needs Gojo gone, and he knows it.

shot.fallback: anime style two young sorcerers in dark school uniforms talking at dusk

lines.text: And with the fanbook calling Gojo unbeatable, I think Kenjaku tries something older and uglier.

shot.fallback: anime style two young sorcerers in dark school uniforms talking at dusk

lines.text: He lets Sukuna be the weapon, and he lets Gojo be the price.

shot.fallback: anime style two young sorcerers in dark school uniforms talking at dusk

lines.text: In that version, Gojo walks into a fight that was never meant for him alone.

shot.fallback: anime style two young sorcerers in dark school uniforms talking at dusk

lines.text: And the cruelest twist is that even then, he would still reach for his friend.

shot.fallback: anime style two young sorcerers in dark school uniforms talking at dusk

lines.text: So the strongest What If isn't about stopping Kenjaku. It's about whether Gojo could ever have said goodbye properly.

shot.fallback: anime style two young sorcerers in dark school uniforms talking at dusk

lines.text: My honest verdict: cremating the body protects the plan, but it also erases the thing that makes Gojo human.

shot.fallback: anime style two young sorcerers in dark school uniforms talking at dusk

lines.text: I could be wrong about where it goes next. But the first link in the chain is canon.

shot.fallback: anime style two young sorcerers in dark school uniforms talking at dusk

lines.text: So here's where I land. Cremation changes Shibuya. Grief explains why it never happened.

shot.fallback: anime style two young sorcerers in dark school uniforms talking at dusk

lines.text: That's why a clean What If still hurts, because the better ending needs a different Gojo.

shot.fallback: anime style two young sorcerers in dark school uniforms talking at dusk
